title: Snowden counting down to Newbury with Wendigo
excerpt: Coral Gold Cup favourite delighted his trainer when winning on his return.
content:
Jamie Snowden expects Wendigo to take a big leap forward from his Carlisle reappearance victory and admitted relief after the handicapper left his mark unchanged for his crack at the Coral Gold Cup.

The Lambourn trainer was delighted by the seven-year-old’s comeback in the Colin Parker Intermediate Chase, with the gelding beating Potters Charm by two and a quarter lengths.

After voicing hopes that the official assessor would “not react too much”, Snowden was delighted to see his mark untouched and said it was now all systems go for his tilt at the Newbury feature on November 28.

“it is always nice to win a race not going up in the handicap, but I suppose there are two ways of looking at everything. The Dan Skelton horse (Doyen Quest) didn’t perform and the second horse (Potters Charm) hasn’t jumped fences in the same manner or the same kind of form as he did over hurdles.

“You can pick holes in the form, but what you can say is that two and a half miles right-handed on good ground is not going to play to our chap’s strengths and you would like to think he will improve for going up in trip and on a left-handed track and hopefully with a little more cut in the ground.”

Bookmakers make Wendigo the general 4-1 favourite for the historic three-and-a-quarter-mile showpiece, while Snowden also predicted his charge will be able to tighten his girths a few notches when he lines up in Berkshire.

He said: “History has always said that Wendigo has been beaten on his seasonal reappearance, whether it be in a bumper a novice hurdle or a novice chase, so you would like to think he will improve for that run going forwards.”
